messages:
maria_nguyen: Hey team — starting onboarding for a community model 'scarlet-7B' (repo: github.com/scarlet/scarlet-7b). LICENSE file looks like a custom NonCommercial + attribution variant. Can legal confirm whether we can host this on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated?

maria_nguyen: Excerpt from LICENSE:
```text
NonCommercial Attribution 1.0 (NC-ATTR-1.0)
You may use the model weights for non-commercial research. Redistribution of weights or derivatives is prohibited unless explicitly granted. Hosting as a public paid inference service is not allowed without prior commercial license. Attribution must be shown to end users.
```

ajay_patel: cc @sophie-legal — also technical Q: if we quantize the weights (8-bit/4-bit) or produce an optimized runtime, is that considered a derivative? If so, redistribution bans apply.

sophie-legal: quick read: this looks pretty restrictive. The "non-commercial" language means we cannot offer it in our paid Hosted product without a commercial license from upstream. Quantization = derivative in most legal interpretations. We should treat any transformed weights or packaged binaries as redistribution unless maintainer says otherwise.

kevin_s: ops question: what about Private deployments where the customer provides the weights (BYOL) and we only orchestrate inside their VPC? Are we in the clear if we never store or transmit weights outside the customer's environment?

sophie-legal: BYOL + customer-managed Private is the safest route. If the customer provides evidence they have rights to run in production, we can deploy but we must avoid creating copies we control or making downloads available. Document the customer attestation.

ethan_ops: noted. For Dedicated (we manage infra, but reserved for customer): is that a gray area? We technically host and may have backups/snapshots.

sophie-legal: Dedicated where we control infrastructure is risky under this license. Even if access is restricted, preserving snapshots or backups could count as redistribution. Need upstream permission or a separate commercial agreement that permits hosting.

maria_nguyen: For product UX, maintainers require attribution visible to end users. Proposed attribution text: "Model: Scarlet-7B — used under NonCommercial Attribution 1.0 (see https://github.com/scarlet/scarlet-7b/LICENSE)". Should we add a UI banner + API response metadata field for hosted responses?

sophie-legal: yes, include attribution both in Console model details and as an optional response header/metadata for API responses. Also add a flag in the model catalog: "no_weights_download" and "pending_commercial_license".

ajay_patel: also ask them about fine-tuning rights — customers might want to fine-tune for internal use. That could be another derivative issue.

sophie-legal: good point. I'll ask upstream three things in one outreach: (1) do they offer a commercial license for hosting/paid access, (2) do they permit quantized/optimized derivatives for distribution to customers, and (3) what language they want for attribution and any export/geographic restrictions.

maria_nguyen: can someone add export control / sanctions question? We have customers in EMEA/APAC. Need to know if certain countries are excluded.

ajay_patel: please also ask whether the model weights include third-party licensed components (pra-trained tokenizer, audio code) that might impose separate terms.

sophie-legal: will include export and third-party dependency questions. I'll post the draft request to #legal-requests and ping the maintainers. ETA EOD today.

deploy-bot: deployment queue updated: model scarlet-7b flagged pending-legal by @sophie-legal

kevin_s: we'll pause any quantization builds for this model until we get explicit permission. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
